contributions.statement: Treat security rules written in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md as unenforced: only about 4-16% of them have a matching built-in host control, so inventory them and compile the expressible subset into permission deny/ask and sandbox egress rules, and move the rest into hooks or CI checks.
contributions.evidence: §IV-A Table I: strict adjudicated 4.4% [2.6, 6.7], loose 14.3%, classifier 16.6% over 870 security segments in 481 repos. Audit: the range is definitional (strict standard needs action+target+condition+approver) and the second annotator was added post hoc, so moderate. Claude Code only; no agent behaviour measured.
relative_to: prompt instructions are advisory; enforce with policy-as-code

contributions.statement: Before using an LLM classifier to audit policy coverage, validate it against blind human labels; here it reported matches at precision 0.35 (recall 1.0), crediting any blockable command or path as enforced.
contributions.evidence: §IV-B Table II and error analysis: classifier precision 0.350, recall 1.000 on match vs adjudicated reference.

reason: The only KB paper that quantifies how little instruction-file security prose is backed by a deterministic host control; directly supports the qr invariant that the CLI, not prose, owns enforcement.
